title: The Midnight, Endless Summer (album cover)
lede: The cover of The Midnight’s first album: a glowing pink neon script over a star-speckled figure, with VHS tracking noise and an on-screen play label.
summary: Pink neon script “The Midnight”, cosmic figure, VHS noise, “▶ ENDLESS SUMMER ©1984”. 2016.

evidence.note: Inspected the 1200 px front-cover image from the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/764fe9af-fff9-478a-bda3-b697e99d9047) in a scratch folder. Not stored. The artist credit comes from The Midnight Wiki; the [Discogs record of the 2016 digital release](https://www.discogs.com/release/8888236) lists no artwork credit.

styles.note: A neon-tube script logotype, a black ground, and VHS tracking lines used as a nostalgic accent: the type and surface side of the style.

context: The Midnight Wiki: *Endless Summer* is the band’s first album, released independently on 5 August 2016. “A small snip of the album artwork (done by Taylor Allen) was revealed in July,” and the full artwork was revealed with the announcement on 25 July. [The Midnight Wiki](https://themidnight.wiki/wiki/Endless_Summer).
Discogs records the original release as a self-released digital file of 5 August 2016, written by Tim McEwan and Tyler Lyle. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/8888236).
observed: The ground is near-black, crossed by faint horizontal lines of video noise. Two bands of heavier static run across the lower third.
A tilted female figure, filled with a star field in cyan, blue, violet, and magenta, rises through the centre.
“The Midnight” crosses the figure in a monoline script drawn as a pink neon tube: a white-hot core, a magenta glow, and a thin cyan and yellow colour offset.
Below, “▶ ENDLESS SUMMER” and “©1984” are set in small, light, pixel-like capitals, like a VCR on-screen display, with a red and cyan colour fringe.
interpretation: The cover shows that VHS artefacts in synthwave are an accent of memory, not decay: the image stays sharp and saturated, and the noise sits on top of it. The false “©1984” date sets the scene in an imagined past.
borrow: Draw a script logotype as a neon tube: a white core line, a wide magenta glow, and a one-pixel cyan offset.
Label a section like a VCR display: a play triangle and small pixel capitals.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The cover art is in copyright (The Midnight / Taylor Allen, 2016).
